title: Clinical course and pathogenicity of a Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis isolate from scimitar oryx (Oryx dammah) in experimentally infected rabbits
author: Maldonado-Castro, Edith
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Acquire and acclimate rabbits
steps.instruction: Obtain three 6‑week‑old female New Zealand rabbits and house them under standard laboratory conditions for acclimation before any manipulation.

steps.title: Prepare MAP inoculum
steps.instruction: Grow the Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis (MAP) isolate from the scimitar oryx and adjust the suspension to contain 1 × 10⁹ colony‑forming units (CFU) per dose for oral administration.

steps.title: Orally infect rabbits
steps.instruction: Administer the MAP suspension orally to each rabbit once daily for three consecutive days, delivering 1 × 10⁹ CFU per rabbit per day.

steps.title: Schedule biweekly sample collection
steps.instruction: Collect blood and fecal samples from each rabbit every two weeks, continuing this schedule for a total of 28 weeks post‑infection.

steps.title: Perform IS900 PCR on blood
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from each blood sample and run IS900 PCR to detect MAP DNA, repeating the assay for every biweekly collection.

steps.title: Perform F57 real‑time PCR on feces
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from each fecal sample and conduct F57 real‑time PCR to quantify MAP shedding, repeating for every biweekly collection.

steps.title: Terminate experiment and harvest tissues
steps.instruction: At 28 weeks post‑infection, euthanize the rabbits and aseptically collect relevant tissues (including vermiform appendix) for downstream analyses.

steps.title: Conduct pathological analysis
steps.instruction: Fix harvested tissues, embed, section, and stain for histopathological examination to assess granulomatous lesions.

steps.title: Perform bacteriological culture
steps.instruction: Inoculate portions of the collected tissues onto appropriate mycobacterial media and incubate under MAP‑specific conditions to isolate viable bacteria.
